transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

I keep getting thoughts that if I miss even one setting, access rule, or warning sign, somebody could get hurt or lose everything. Part of me knows that sounds irrational, but it feels like it would be my fault, and I can’t just let it go.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking things or doing specific routines to try to prevent those bad things from happening?

Yes. I reread deployment plans, audit logs, old messages—sometimes the same things over and over. I check door locks too. In my head I’ll count through steps until it feels safe enough. If I stop before it feels complete, I get panicky, and I’ve stayed at the office for hours after everyone else leaves just checking.

latest_inference.note: Patient exhibits classic obsessions (irrational fear of harm/responsibility) and compulsions (repeated checking of logs, door locks, mental counting rituals) causing significant distress and time loss, ruling out GAD (F41.1) and OCPD (F60.5).
